heading: In 2012, NFL legend Joe Thomas bought a 1,200-acre Wisconsin farm with five cows and a bull; 14 years later, Hall of Fame Farms spans 4,100 acres and raises hundreds of cattle, including Wagyu
author: TOI World Desk / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Sep 21, 2026, 18:20 IST
paragraphs: Former Cleveland Browns star Joe Thomas has taken an unexpected turn after retiring from football, trading the NFL field for life on a Wisconsin farm
The Pro Football Hall of Famer is the owner of Hall of Fame Farms, a cattle operation located in the state’s Driftless Region
Thomas spent 11 seasons with the Browns before retiring in 2018 and was inducted into the Hall of Fame in 2023
According to Fox News, his interest in farming grew while he was still playing, eventually leading him to build a substantial agricultural operation with his family

Farm Progress has also reported on Thomas’ work on the farm and his approach to raising cattle.From football to farmingThomas, who grew up in Wisconsin, has spoken about wanting to own land long before his NFL career ended

He purchased the original property in 2012, while still playing for Cleveland, and initially started with just a handful of cattle.What began as a family farm eventually developed into a much larger agricultural operation

Fox News reported in September 2026 that the property has grown from the original 1,200 acres to roughly 4,100 acres and now includes hundreds of cattle, with Wagyu increasingly becoming a focus of the business
The transition also reflects a broader change in Thomas’ life after football
Following his retirement, he became increasingly interested in food, nutrition and the way cattle are raised

Farm Progress reported earlier this year that Thomas and his farm team emphasize nutrition and individual attention when caring for the herd.A different kind of Hall of Fame careerThomas’ football résumé gives the farm its distinctive name
Selected third overall by the Cleveland Browns in the 2007 NFL Draft, he played his entire 11-season career in Cleveland
Thomas made 10 consecutive Pro Bowls, earned six first-team All-Pro selections and played 10,363 consecutive offensive snaps
The Pro Football Hall of Fame lists him as a member of its Class of 2023.That reputation for consistency has now become part of the identity of his agricultural business

Hall of Fame Farms presents the operation as a long-term family project rather than simply a celebrity venture, with Thomas and his wife, Annie, raising their children around the farm.What happens on the farmThe cattle operation places a significant emphasis on producing both Wagyu and Certified Angus beef varieties

As reported by Hall of Fame Farms, the cattle are raised on pasture before entering a corn-finishing phase, while the farm also utilizes carefully selected genetics combined with a tailored nutrition programme that was developed in collaboration with a dedicated cattle nutritionist

In addition to this, the company proudly claims to work with Full Blood Wagyu genetics, ensuring high-quality meat production.The approach taken by the farm is fundamentally centred around low-stress handling techniques and a strong focus on comprehensive animal care to promote the well-being of the cattle
As highlighted by Farm Progress, Thomas’ dedicated team prioritizes nutritional needs and provides personalized care for each individual animal within their herd
Currently, the business offers a diverse array of beef products to consumers, which includes a selection of Wagyu steaks, Certified Angus beef, a variety of smoked meats, and beef tallow

Furthermore, the farm has established an online platform that enables customers to conveniently order specific cuts of meat directly from the brand.Building something beyond footballFor Thomas, farming represents a second chapter rather than a complete break from his sporting career
The precision and consistency that defined his time in the NFL have become part of how he describes his approach to cattle.The setting is also central to the project

Hall of Fame Farms sits among the rolling hills and pastureland of Wisconsin’s Driftless Region, where Thomas has gradually turned a property bought during his playing days into a family-run agricultural business.His football career ended in 2018, but the next chapter has continued to grow
